stories.headline: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.5-Omni, Claims 215 SOTA Wins Over Gemini 3.1 Pro

key_facts.fact: Alibaba released Qwen3.5-Omni, a fully omnimodal LLM supporting text, image, audio, and video understanding plus text and speech generation.
The Plus variant claims to surpass Gemini 3.1 Pro on audio benchmarks and achieves 215 state-of-the-art results across benchmarks.
The model supports over 10 hours of audio input and features audio-visual vibe coding, where users can point a camera at something and describe what they want built.
The model includes real-time web search capabilities built in.

stories.headline: California Gov. Newsom Signs First-of-Its-Kind AI Safety and Privacy Executive Order

key_facts.fact: Governor Newsom signed an executive order requiring AI companies contracting with California to demonstrate responsible policies and meet rigorous privacy and security standards.
The order is framed as a contrast to the Trump administration, which has been rolling back federal AI protections and contracting standards.
The order also commits to expanding California's use of GenAI to deliver improved state services, including a new AI-directed tool to help Californians navigate government.
California is described as the 4th largest economy in the world, making its procurement standards significant for the AI industry.

stories.headline: Microsoft Launches Copilot Cowork and Multi-Model Critique System Using Claude and GPT

key_facts.fact: Microsoft rolled out Copilot Cowork to its Frontier early access program, enabling long-running, multi-step tasks with tool use, file access, calendar planning, and daily briefings.
The new Critique feature has one AI model (Claude) draft research while a second model (GPT) reviews it, pulling from both Anthropic and OpenAI models.
Microsoft claims the Critique agent outperforms Perplexity with Claude Opus 4.6 by 7 points on deep research benchmarks, though it doesn't compare against OpenAI's GPT-5-based Deep Research.
A new Model Council feature lets users compare answers from different AI models side by side to see where they agree or differ.

stories.headline: Leaked Coatue Slides Project Anthropic at $2 Trillion Valuation by 2030

key_facts.fact: A leaked January 2026 Coatue presentation projected Anthropic would reach a $1.995 trillion valuation by 2030 and $2.413 trillion by 2031.
Coatue estimated Anthropic would lose $14 billion in EBITDA on $18 billion in revenue in 2026, ending the year with $30 billion in annualized run-rate revenue.
Anthropic is currently reported at $19 billion in ARR, suggesting it is running ahead of Coatue's January projections.
In February, Coatue co-led a $30 billion Series G investment in Anthropic that valued it at $380 billion.

stories.headline: South Korean AI Chip Startup Rebellions Raises $400M at $2.34B Valuation Ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: Rebellions raised $400 million in a pre-IPO round led by Mirae Asset Financial Group and the Korea National Growth Fund, bringing total funding to $850 million.
The company raised $650 million of its $850 million total in just the last six months, with its valuation at approximately $2.34 billion.
Rebellions designs AI inference chips (fabless) and announced new RebelRack and RebelPOD products for rack-scale AI infrastructure.
The company has recently established entities in the US, Japan, Saudi Arabia, and Taiwan as part of an aggressive global expansion.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot Injected Ads Into 11,000+ Pull Requests, Disabled After Backlash

key_facts.fact: GitHub Copilot was found injecting promotional 'product tips' referencing Raycast into pull request descriptions, with the same text found in over 11,000 pull requests.
After widespread developer backlash, GitHub disabled product tips entirely, with product manager Martin Woodward calling it a mistake rather than paid advertising.
GitHub explained the tips were originally included in Copilot-originated PRs but expanded problematically when Copilot gained the ability to work on any PR.

stories.headline: Quinnipiac Poll: 55% of Americans Say AI Will Do More Harm Than Good

key_facts.fact: 55% of Americans say AI will do more harm than good in their day-to-day lives, and 80% are 'very concerned' or 'somewhat concerned' about AI.
65% oppose building data centers in their community, with 72% of opponents citing electricity costs as a key concern.
Nearly 70% think AI will cut jobs, with Gen Z the most pessimistic generation about AI's impact on employment.
AI job loss concerns are shared roughly equally between blue collar (73%) and white collar (71%) workers.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches AI Safety Bug Bounty With Up to $7,500 Payouts

key_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced a new Safety Bug Bounty program paying up to $7,500 for AI-specific safety vulnerabilities, including harmful model behavior at scale and proprietary information leaks.
The program targets agentic products including the Atlas Browser and Codex vibe-coding agent, as well as MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations.
The Safety Bug Bounty complements OpenAI's existing Security Bug Bounty which has maximum rewards of $100,000 and has paid out on 417 bugs.
OpenAI is specifically looking for MCP vulnerabilities where systems can be tricked, misconfigured, or bypassed to cause unauthorized data access or impersonated actions.

stories.headline: Qodo Raises $70M Series B for AI Code Verification as AI-Generated Code Scales

key_facts.fact: Qodo raised a $70 million Series B led by Qumra Capital, bringing total funding to $120 million, with investors including OpenAI's Peter Welinder and Meta's Clara Shih.
Qodo ranked #1 on Martian's Code Review Bench, scoring 64.3% — more than 10 points ahead of the next competitor and 25 points ahead of Claude Code Review.
Clients include Nvidia, Walmart, Red Hat, Intuit, and Texas Instruments, plus high-growth firms like Monday.com and JFrog.
A recent survey shows 95% of developers don't fully trust AI-generated code, yet only 48% consistently review it before committing.

stories.headline: Meta Releases Hyperagents, an AI Framework That Can Rewrite Its Own Code

key_facts.fact: Meta released Hyperagents, a framework that unifies task-solving and meta-improvement into a single editable Python program, enabling AI agents to autonomously modify their own source code.
Hyperagents extend the Darwin Godel Machine (DGM) by making all meta-procedures editable, allowing the meta agent to rewrite its own modification code, solving infinite meta-level regress.
The system is domain-agnostic, demonstrating improved performance across robotics, math grading, and academic paper review without task-specific alignment.
The system runs over 100 experiments per iteration using LLM-driven latent-space search to iteratively optimize its code.

stories.headline: Google Releases Agent Development Kit for Java 1.0 With A2A Protocol Support

key_facts.fact: Google released version 1.0.0 of the Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java, expanding the multi-language ADK ecosystem (Python, Java, Go, TypeScript).
Key features include Google Maps and URL context grounding tools, a centralized plugin architecture, event compaction for context window management, and Human-in-the-Loop workflows.
The release includes native support for the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, enabling agents built in different languages and frameworks to communicate seamlessly.

stories.headline: TSMC Fully Booked at 2nm Through 2028, Opening Door for Samsung Foundry

key_facts.fact: TSMC's 2nm process is fully booked through 2028 with orders from Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm, and Apple. Even its Arizona fab targeting 2030 production is reportedly largely reserved.
Samsung, the only other company capable of 2nm production, has raised yields to around 60% and is securing orders from Tesla, Apple, and expanding engagement with Nvidia.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confirmed Samsung is producing the Grok 3 language processing unit using its 4nm process.
TSMC holds 72% of the global foundry market vs Samsung's 7%, but at sub-5nm nodes it is effectively a duopoly.
Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab is set to begin operations in the second half of 2026.

stories.headline: Nebius Announces $10B, 310MW AI Data Center in Finland, One of Europe's Largest

key_facts.fact: Amsterdam-based Nebius announced a 310-megawatt data center in Lappeenranta, Finland, with an estimated value exceeding $10 billion.
The facility is being built by Finnish developer Polarnode and capacity is due to come online in phases from 2027.
Nebius has recently won supply contracts worth more than $40 billion with Microsoft and Meta.
The site will cover roughly 10% of Nebius' contracted capacity, which targets 3+ gigawatts by end of 2026.
Finland was chosen for its low energy prices, renewable electricity supply, and cold climate that reduces cooling costs.

stories.headline: Airbus 'Bird of Prey' Counter-Drone Interceptor Completes First Demo Flight in Germany

key_facts.fact: The Airbus Bird of Prey interceptor drone completed its first demonstration flight at a military training area in northern Germany on March 30.
The drone autonomously searched, detected, and classified a kamikaze drone, then engaged it with a Mark I air-to-air missile from startup Frankenburg Technologies.

The prototype has a 2.5m wingspan, 160kg max takeoff weight, and can carry up to 8 missiles in the operational version. The Mark I missiles weigh under 2kg and are the lightest guided interceptors ever developed.
The demo took place just nine months after the project started. Airbus and Frankenburg plan live warhead tests throughout 2026.

stories.headline: Varda Launches W-6 Mission to Advance Autonomous Hypersonic Reentry Capabilities

key_facts.fact: Varda Space Industries launched its W-6 vehicle on SpaceX's Transporter-16 on March 30, its sixth mission overall and first of 2026.
W-6 carries an autonomous navigation system that uses onboard imagery to identify resident space objects for precise position determination during hypersonic flight.
The mission carries a Sandia National Lab nose tile with advanced thermal protection materials and two instrumented shoulder tiles collecting data for NASA.
The mission is funded through a partnership between the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) and commercial space entities.

stories.headline: Micron Shares Crash 30% Since Earnings as AI Memory Chip Shortage Deepens

key_facts.fact: Micron shares fell 10% on Monday March 30, bringing total decline to 30% since its earnings report on March 18.
CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said key customers only receive 'half to two-thirds of their requirements' due to the supply crunch driven by AI demand.
SanDisk fell 7% and Western Digital dropped 9% as the sell-off spread across memory makers.
Neocloud companies CoreWeave and Nebius were each down about 8% amid broader tech sell-off driven by rising oil prices from the Iran war.

stories.headline: SpaceX Starlink Satellite Explodes in Orbit, Second Such Incident Since December

key_facts.fact: SpaceX lost contact with Starlink satellite 34343 after an 'anomaly' on Sunday March 29 at approximately 560km altitude.
Space-tracking company Leo Labs detected 'tens of objects' near the satellite, suggesting it broke apart or exploded.
SpaceX says the event poses no risk to the ISS, its crew, or the upcoming Artemis II mission. Debris expected to burn up within weeks.
This is the second similar incident since December, when SpaceX also suddenly lost a satellite that seemingly exploded.
Over 24,000 objects are tracked in low Earth orbit, including about 10,000 Starlink satellites. SpaceX recently requested FCC approval for up to one million AI satellites.

stories.headline: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Robot Returns to Hollywood Diner With Food Runner Ambitions

key_facts.fact: Tesla's Optimus Gen 3 robot is returning to the Tesla Diner on Santa Monica Boulevard in Hollywood, as announced via @Tesla_Optimus on March 30.
Gen 3 Optimus features 50 total actuators and 22 degrees of freedom per hand, with Tesla's AI5 chip and Grok-powered voice interaction.
Musk has ambitions for Optimus to serve as a food runner in 2026, delivering meals to cars at Supercharger stalls.
Tesla is converting its Fremont Model S and Model X production lines to build Optimus robots, after discontinuing those vehicle models.

stories.headline: London AI Chip Startup Fractile in Talks to Raise $200M at $1B Unicorn Valuation

key_facts.fact: Fractile is in discussions with Accel and early backer Oxford Science Enterprises to raise over $200M at a $1B valuation.
Founded in 2022, Fractile builds chips for AI inference that it says work faster and cheaper than Nvidia's GPUs. Backers include NATO Innovation Fund and Arm cofounder Hermann Hauser.
The UK AI minister recently announced Fractile would invest £100M building operations in London and Bristol, including a new engineering facility.
The company raised $15M in a 2024 seed round and a further $22.5M from NIF, Kindred, and OSE.

stories.headline: Fermi Shares Plunge 25% on $486M Loss, No Tenant for Nuclear AI Data Center Project

key_facts.fact: Fermi shares fell about 25% on Monday after reporting a GAAP net loss of $486.4M ($1.13/share), exceeding analyst expectations of $366.5M.
The company, which went public in October, is now down roughly 80% from its IPO level and has yet to generate revenue.
A key nonbinding letter of intent to lease part of its Project Matador nuclear-powered data center site was terminated in December without a replacement.
Fermi, co-founded by former US Energy Secretary Rick Perry, is building Project Matador to supply nuclear energy to AI data centers. Cash stood at $408.5M at end of Q4.

stories.headline: Gulf States Press Trump to Continue Iran War Until Islamic Regime Falls

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain asked Trump to continue attacks against Iran until the regime is crippled enough for regime change or stops being a regional threat, per AP report citing Gulf and Israeli officials
Saudi Arabia and UAE are leading the push to increase military pressure on Tehran, while Oman and Qatar maintain a more neutral stance favoring diplomacy
Saudi Arabia believes any negotiated deal would be insufficient and Iran's nuclear program must be fully destroyed before talks can begin
Netanyahu said the war is 'beyond its halfway point' and proposed rerouting Gulf energy pipelines through Saudi Arabia to the Red Sea and Mediterranean, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz

stories.headline: Iran-US Peace Talks Stall: 15-Point Plan Meets Five Iranian Counter-Demands

key_facts.fact: The US proposed a 15-point plan delivered to Iran via Pakistan, but no face-to-face meeting has been set despite Pakistan's offer to host discussions; Iran denies negotiations are taking place
US demands include: Iran cannot enrich uranium on its soil, must surrender 10,000 kg of fissile material, and accept oversight mechanisms — all red lines for Tehran

Iran countered with five demands: halt to 'aggression and assassinations,' mechanisms to prevent re-imposition of war, reparations, and recognition of Iran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz (which carries 20%+ of global oil)
Trump claimed 'great progress' on Truth Social; Iran's Foreign Affairs spokesperson called US demands 'very excessive, unrealistic and irrational' and denied any negotiations
Pakistan army chief Syed Asim Munir is the key intermediary; top diplomats from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt have held talks about possible talks

Iran allowed 20 ships through the Strait of Hormuz plus 10 last week, but still controls the passageway; Secretary Rubio questioned who is making decisions in Iran, noting no one has seen new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei

stories.headline: Oil Caps Historic Month: Brent Up 56%, US Crude Tops $100 for First Time Since 2022

key_facts.fact: Brent crude on track for a 56% rise in March — the largest monthly gain on record — trading at $113.05/barrel
US WTI crude settled above $100/barrel for the first time since July 2022, closing just below $103 after a 3%+ daily gain on Monday
US WTI headed for a monthly rise of roughly 54%, the most in nearly six years
Average US retail gasoline prices hovering just below $4/gallon as the Iran war enters its fifth week
Markets briefly calmed after WSJ reported Trump told aides he's willing to end the military campaign even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed

stories.headline: Powell: Fed Can 'Wait and See' as Iran War Creates Inflation-Jobs Tension

key_facts.fact: Speaking at Harvard, Powell said the Fed can wait to see how the Iran war affects the economy, noting policymakers typically look through oil price shocks
Powell acknowledged tension between the Fed's two mandates: downside risk to jobs suggests keeping rates low, upside risk to inflation suggests otherwise
Rate hike bets have 'all but disappeared' after Powell's remarks; the Fed is now expected to hold rates this year vs. 50+ bps of cuts priced in before the war began
Inflation has run above the 2% target for about five years through a series of shocks (COVID, tariffs, and now energy); Powell said 'no one knows how big' the energy shock will be
The Fed held rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% earlier this month; Powell's leadership term ends May 15, with Trump nominee Kevin Warsh set to succeed him

stories.headline: Asian Markets Head for Steepest Monthly Decline Since 2020 on War Fears

key_facts.fact: MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index on track for over 13% monthly fall, the most substantial decline since March 2020
Japan's Nikkei set to lose nearly 13% this month; South Korea's Kospi headed for over 18% monthly decline — the most since 2008
India's rupee, Indonesia's rupiah, and the Philippine peso all hit record lows against the dollar in March amid heavy selling of Asian currencies
US dollar headed for biggest monthly gain since July, up roughly 2.9% against a basket of currencies; spot gold at $4,564.73/oz
US 2-year Treasury yield set to rise over 40 bps this month (largest since Oct 2024); 10-year yield up about 36 bps (largest since Dec 2024) as rate hike expectations shifted

stories.headline: SDNY Prosecutors Probe Prediction Market Insider Trading, Meet Polymarket

key_facts.fact: SDNY securities and commodities fraud unit chiefs met with Polymarket representatives to discuss how insider trading, anti-money laundering, and anti-fraud laws apply to prediction market activity
Prosecutors are investigating specific lucrative trades including bets on the timing of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro's capture and well-timed Iran war bets
SDNY US Attorney Jay Clayton warned at a securities law conference that he believes there will be criminal cases involving prediction market activity
Arizona filed the first criminal charges against Kalshi for allegedly operating an illegal gambling business; Kalshi denies wrongdoing and calls the charges 'paper thin'
Polymarket issued new rules banning trades on confidential information; Kalshi announced rules blocking politicians from trading on their own campaigns and athletes from trading in their leagues

stories.headline: FDA Approves High-Dose Spinraza for Spinal Muscular Atrophy

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Biogen's high-dose (50mg) Spinraza formulation for spinal muscular atrophy, reversing a surprise rejection in September 2025 that cited manufacturing concerns
New regimen requires two 50mg loading doses 14 days apart plus 28mg maintenance every four months, replacing four 12mg induction doses — significantly faster loading
Spinraza sales peaked at $2.097B in 2019 but slumped below $1.55B in 2025 after Roche's competing oral SMA drug Evrysdi won FDA approval; high-dose approval could reinvigorate the franchise
Approval was backed by Phase 2/3 DEVOTE study showing significantly better motor skill outcomes than sham control; updated data also showed improvements in event-free survival

stories.headline: Micron Plunges 10%, Down 30% in Two Weeks as Memory Sector Tumbles

key_facts.fact: Micron shares fell 10% on Monday, extending a post-earnings selloff to 30% since its March 18 earnings report despite strong Q2 results
Memory sector peers SanDisk and Western Digital fell 7% and 9% respectively; neocloud companies CoreWeave and Nebius each dropped about 8%
CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said key customers receive only 'half to two-thirds of their requirements' due to an AI-driven supply crunch; Micron stock is up 270% from a year ago but only 2% YTD
